papers.grim_cells_not_itemised: None: the Appendix itemises every granularity error. Age, height and weight were deliberately excluded from GRIM testing by the critics.
papers.other_tests_flagged: GRIMMER: 1 SD (Table 2, $8, middle piece very enjoyable, SD 1.22, N = 26). Test statistics/p values: 7 (Table 1 Age F and p, Number in group F and p; Table 2 three middle-piece F statistics). Degrees of freedom: 1 impossible (F[1,122] implies 124 diners) and 3 changing dfs in the Table 3 text.
papers.n_question: Serious. The printed Table 2 header gives N = 62 ($4) / 60 ($8) for every row; the critics instead used per-row Ns inferred from Article 2's regression models (41/26 for middle-piece rows, 47/38 for last-piece rows). At the printed header n, 6.16 (N = 62) and both 7.97 cells (N = 60) are GRIM-CONSISTENT, so those three labels hold only under the critics' cross-article inference. The 2017 erratum and the data release show every row had its own n (Table 1: 64-70; Table 2: 39-63 at $4, 29-61 at $8), usually LARGER than printed; at those true ns the flagged means become consistent, except the two gender percentages whose printed values themselves were later changed (to 60.0 and 51.5). So the GRIM failures are real inconsistencies with the printed n, caused mainly by misreported n (plus one duplicated row).
papers.notes: Itemised cells copied from the Appendix of the BMC Nutrition article (read via Europe PMC full-text XML, PMC7050813); mean strings cross-checked against the critics' own copy-pasted transcription (github.com/OmnesRes/pizzapizza, Python/paper1_table1.txt and paper1_table2.txt) and the 'Original Table' reproductions in 'Statistical infarction'. Every listed cell recomputes as GRIM-inconsistent at the critics' n (field 'recheck'). Extra keys per cell: value_kind, recheck (our recomputation), doubt.
